text.p: The Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) 20-share index fell on Wednesday dragged down by an adjusted share price in Kenya's leading supermarket chain, Uchumi, bourse officials said.
The index fell 18.44 points to stand 3027.12. Turnover was posted at 5.725 million shillings on 199,476 shares from 15.872 million shillings on 506,453 shares on Tuesday.
"Uchumi Supermarket announced a final dividend of 4.0 shillings on October 9 and a bonus issue of one share for every two shares," an official said.
The closing price for Uchumi Supermarket was 49.50 up from 39.50 on Tuesday.
"As a result of the bonus issue, the adjusted share price fell to 33 shilling from 49.50 thus partly contributing to the drop in the index," a senior broker told Reuters.
"Wednesday saw a quiet trading session with very few small lots being dealt ahead of a public holiday on Thursday," the official said.
Among the plantations, Brooke Bond rose a shilling to 179, Rea Vipingo to 10.85 from 10.95 while Kakuzi remained unchanged at 95.
Kenya Airways traded 51,964 shares at 9.80 from 9.90, Car & General fell to 19.50 from 20 while Nation Printers & Publishers was steady at 106.
Barclays Bank rose to 98.50 from 98, Kenya Commercial Bank gained to 55 from 54 and National Bank of Kenya eased to 15.70 from 15.80.
Bourse officials said that with few people buying and even fewer selling, prices in some counters tended to rise.
Oil concern Total Kenya eased to 71.50 from 72 while foreign investors dealt 800 shares of Firestone East Africa at 25 shillings.
